title: Rights and Responsibilities — Being a Good Citizen Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of rights, responsibilities, and good citizenship!

questions.question: According to the Declaration of Independence, where do our rights come from?
questions.explanation: The Declaration of Independence states that our rights are given to us by our Creator. This means our rights come from God, not from any government.

questions.question: What does the word 'unalienable' mean when talking about our rights?
options: They can be changed by voting
questions.explanation: Unalienable means our rights cannot be taken away. Because God gave them to us, no government has the authority to remove them.

questions.question: What is the Bill of Rights?
options: A list of taxes citizens must pay
The first ten amendments to the Constitution
A list of things citizens must do
The first chapter of the Bible
questions.explanation: The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the Constitution. It protects our God-given freedoms by limiting what the government can do.

questions.question: Which freedom is protected by the First Amendment?
options: The right to drive a car
The right to a free education
Freedom to travel to other countries
questions.explanation: The First Amendment protects five freedoms: religion, speech, the press, assembly, and petition. Freedom of religion was listed first because the Founders considered it the most important.

questions.question: What is the difference between a civic duty and a civic responsibility?
options: Duties are for adults; responsibilities are for children
Duties are required by law; responsibilities are voluntary
Duties are about money; responsibilities are about time
questions.explanation: Civic duties are required by law (like obeying laws and paying taxes), while civic responsibilities are voluntary actions good citizens should do (like voting and volunteering).

questions.question: What Bible verse teaches us to 'love your neighbor as yourself'?
questions.explanation: Matthew 22:39 records Jesus teaching the second greatest commandment: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Community service is one way we put this commandment into action.

questions.question: Who is the leader of a state government?
questions.explanation: The governor is the leader of a state government, similar to how the President leads the federal government.

questions.question: Why did the Founders believe citizens need to be informed?
options: So they can pass school tests
So they can protect their freedoms and make wise decisions
So they can argue with their neighbors
questions.explanation: The Founders believed that an informed citizenry is essential for a free republic. Citizens need to know what is happening so they can protect their freedoms and hold leaders accountable.
